title: Access Token Exchange
means: code is now exchanged for the user's access token by making a POST request to the token URL with the following parameters: grant_type - must be set to authorization_code, code - the code from the querystring, redirect_uri - the redirect_uri associated with this authorization. In response, you will receive: Access Token Response

title: Access Token Exchange: grant_type, refused as RFC 6749 section 5.2 states (Discord's OAuth2 page says it must be authorization_code and refers implementers to RFC 6749; the 400 and its error body are where that page stops)
means: The authorization server responds with an HTTP 400 (Bad Request) status code (unless specified otherwise) and includes the following parameters with the response: error REQUIRED. A single ASCII [USASCII] error code from the following: ... unsupported_grant_type The authorization grant type is not supported by the authorization server.

title: Refresh Token Exchange
means: To refresh, make another POST request to the token URL with the following parameters: grant_type - must be set to refresh_token, refresh_token - the user's refresh token. Boom; fresh access token response!

title: Client Credentials Token Request
means: By making a POST request to the token URL with a grant type of client_credentials, using Basic authentication with your client id as the username and your client secret as the password, you will be returned an access token for the bot owner.

title: Extended Bot Authorization Access Token
means: When you retrieve the user's access token, you'll also receive information about the guild to which your bot was added

title: Webhook Token Response
means: The URL will contain the code querystring parameter which should be exchanged for an access token. In return, you will receive a slightly modified token response
